title: Bidirectional A*: Find Routes in Napoli Faster!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race across a real street-map grid from start to goal—meeting in the middle to slash search effort. This visualization shows how informed graph search can stay optimal while exploring dramatically fewer nodes.
ig_caption:
🚦🗺️ Napoli (Vomero) street-maps, but with brains: Bidirectional A*.

✨ How it works (the nerdy magic): Bidirectional A* runs two A* searches simultaneously—one forward from the start and one backward from the destination. Each side uses a heuristic to estimate distance-to-go, while the two frontiers efficiently converge at a meeting point, often reducing expansions versus classic single-direction A*.

📈 Graph theory on real roads: We model streets as a weighted graph (intersections = nodes, road segments = edges). Costs can represent distance/time, and the heuristic guides exploration to the most promising regions. When the forward and backward searches touch, we stitch the partial paths into the globally shortest route (under consistent conditions).

⚡ In this reel: notice the wavefronts shrinking as the algorithm learns “where the answer is” from both directions.

👉 Want the next city + algorithm combo? Comment your pick, and if you learn something, share this with a fellow developer who loves shortest paths! 💬❤️
fb_caption:
🚍🗺️ In Naples (Vomero), we visualize Bidirectional A* to show how graph search can be both fast and optimal. Instead of exploring outward from only one start point, it searches from the start and the goal at the same time—shrinking the work until the paths meet.
